results.title: CM Chandrababu Naidu accuses YSRCP chief Jagan of 'damaging' Andhra's brand image
results.description: Amaravati, Oct 24 (IANS) Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu on Saturday launched a scathing attack on YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, accusing him of "damaging" the brand image of the state and alleging that he lacks political, moral and family values. Addressing a press conference, CM Naidu expressed serious concern over "deliberate attempts to damage" the prestige and brand image of Andhra Pradesh. "Jagan Mohan Reddy speaks an incomprehensible language and is consistently working with the sole agenda of claiming that law and order has collapsed in the state, purely to demand President’s Rule and extract political mileage," he alleged. CM Naidu referred to Jagan as a "prolonged litigant" operating under the "guise of politics". Custom Ad: Multiplex "Jagan follows a routine of filing repetitive court petitions and lunch motions, only to see them postponed, while systematically propagating untruths through extended press conferences after arriving from Bengaluru," he remarked. Moreover, Chief Minister Naidu firmly rejected allegations that YSRCP candidates were prevented from participating in the nomination process for the upcoming local body polls, pointing out that police personnel actively provided security and transported candidates in official vehicles to facilitate their filings. He cited the statement of YSRCP’s former Deputy Speaker from Bapatla, Kona Raghupathi, who publicly confirmed that the nominations concluded smoothly without hindrance. CM Naidu also condemned Jagan Mohan Reddy’s "deceitful posture" and recalled the "grim reality" of the 2021 Covid pandemic, criticising how school teachers were forced into guarding and managing queues outside liquor outlets during the period. Highlighting that the excessive uncontested victories in 2021, including 24 per cent of MPTCs statewide and massive unanimous sweeps in Kadapa, were achieved through "intimidation and brute force", the Chief Minister urged the public to recognise the "habitual pattern of falsehoods designed to mislead the state". Further, the Andhra Pradesh CM accused the YSR Congress Party chief of treating his own mother and sister "unfairly" over property disputes and questioned his refusal to provide Yelahanka Palace for his niece’s wedding. Asserting that Jagan’s sister YS Sharmila also has a share in the family property, the Chief Minister accused him of obstructing his niece’s wedding, comparing his behaviour to that of the Hindu mythology demon king 'Kansa'. Further, CM Naidu urged people to understand how "dangerous" the YSPCP chief’s mindset could be for the state and alleged that the latter's overall approach was driven by "destruction". --IANS cg/uk

results.title: Bihar govt intensifies food safety raids, seizes spoiled food and expired products
results.description: Patna, Oct 24 (IANS) Bihar’s Food Safety Department has intensified inspections across the state on the initiative of Health Minister Nishant Kumar to ensure the availability of safe, hygienic and quality food products. So far, 531 food establishments have been inspected under a special statewide campaign. The department has suspended the licences of two establishments and initiated prosecution proceedings against 15 others for violations of food safety standards. The inspections have led to action against spoiled paneer, foul-smelling sweets, expired milk and other food products, as well as used and burnt cooking oil. Custom Ad: Multiplex Patna recorded the highest number of inspections, with 87 establishments examined. Nishant Kumar has directed officials to ensure strict compliance with food safety regulations, making it clear that public health cannot be compromised. Food business operators must maintain hygiene, ensure proper storage, meet quality standards and hold valid licences. Violations will invite legal action. In Patna, inspections covered hotels, restaurants, sweet shops, dairies, fast-food outlets, packaged drinking water units and online food retailers. In Sampatchak, Gaurichak and nearby areas, water was seized from packaged drinking water units operating without valid licences. Authorities also detected unauthorised packaging and the use of brand labels without proper authorisation. Operations at the affected units were stopped, and samples were sent for laboratory testing. At Santosh Sweets in Vijay Nagar, officials seized 3,344 kg of milk cake and 112 kg of peda, valued at approximately Rs 5.24 lakh. Action was also taken against 170 kg of foul-smelling sweets and paneer at Govardhan Sweets. Across Patna district, enforcement measures involved around 15,340 litres of packaged drinking water, 155 kg of gulab jamun, 96 kg of rasgulla and other food products. Inspections at hotels, including Gargi Grand, Pataliputra Exotica, The Panase and Hotel Maurya, revealed deficiencies in kitchen hygiene, food storage, staff health certificates and water quality testing. In some establishments, vegetarian and non-vegetarian food items were stored together. The establishments were given 14 days to rectify the shortcomings. During inspections on October 21, officials found serious violations at outlets of Barbeque Nation, KFC and Pizza Hut. At Barbeque Nation on Buddha Marg, 30 kg of foul-smelling paneer and 4 kg of rice were seized and destroyed, while the use of 15 kg of pre-packaged chicken was prohibited. At its Fraser Road outlet, insects were found in bread packets, and 20 litres of used cooking oil were destroyed. At KFC on Boring Canal Road, the use of 835 plastic cups intended for industrial use was prohibited. On October 22, officials seized and destroyed 40 litres of expired Amul milk at a Blinkit store. At a 9-to-9 store in SK Nagar, they seized and destroyed 120 litres of expired ghee, 49 kg each of whole wheat flour and refined flour, and 6 kg of spices. Beyond Patna, inspections over the past three months covered 41 establishments in Rohtas, 40 in Saran, 37 in Gopalganj, 27 in Siwan, 26 in Gaya, 24 in Vaishali and 20 in Muzaffarpur. The report recorded no inspections in Sheikhpura and Sheohar. In Vaishali, 22,992 litres of packaged drinking water were seized from units operating without valid licences. In Bidupur, 328 kg of adulterated paneer worth Rs 85,280 was destroyed. Officials also acted against 105 kg of paneer, gulab jamun and doda sweets in Muzaffarpur, while 72 kg of spoiled paneer was destroyed in West Champaran. Similar enforcement actions were reported in Samastipur, Saharsa, Siwan, Gopalganj, Munger, Purnea, Madhepura, Rohtas and Kaimur. In Hajipur, a hotel’s licence was suspended and its operations halted after officials found its kitchen unhygienic. The department said violations could attract imprisonment of up to three months and a fine of up to Rs 3 lakh under the applicable provisions. To strengthen enforcement, qualified Health Department officials have been appointed as Food Safety Officers after 14 days of foundational training and 26 days of on-the-job training. Officials have been directed to constitute inspection teams and upload action reports to the FoSCoS portal. The department said inspections would continue, with particular focus on milk and dairy products, sweets, edible oils, spices, hotels, restaurants and online food businesses. --IANS ajk/dan

results.title: Punjab Congress alleges scam of Rs 4,000 crore in paddy procurement
results.description: Chandigarh, Oct 24 (IANS) Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President Pargat Singh on Saturday visited the grain market in Kukkar Pind village in Jalandhar to assess the status of paddy procurement and lifting. During the visit, he levelled allegations against the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government, accusing it of a scam of approximately Rs 4,000 crore in paddy procurement. He alleged that the government had entered into a purported deal of Rs 200 per gunny bag involving rice millers and private agencies. He said the government's failure to undertake timely and effective planning had left farmers struggling in the mandis. After listening to farmers’ grievances, Pargat Singh contacted officials of the Food and Supplies Department over the phone and reprimanded them over delays in procurement and lifting. He said there was a significant gap between the government's claims and the ground reality. Despite paddy arriving at the mandis, adequate arrangements for procurement and lifting had not been made, leaving farmers to bear the consequences. Custom Ad: Multiplex In a statement, Pargat Singh alleged that instead of ensuring an organised and efficient lifting process, the government had awarded a contract to a favoured rice mill, creating scope for arbitrary practices. He questioned why the government had chosen to rely on a single agency when adequate arrangements were needed for both procurement and lifting. He expressed concern that such arrangements could lead to confrontations between farmers and commission agents, while farmers were being unnecessarily harassed in their efforts to sell their produce. Responding to questions about the reported suspension of paddy procurement, Pargat Singh said Punjab had a procurement target of approximately 18 million metric tons. He questioned how the government could justify telling farmers that procurement was being stopped when the target had not yet been achieved. He said the situation exposed the government's failure and lack of foresight in planning. He demanded immediate and effective measures to ensure the timely procurement of farmers’ produce and its prompt lifting from the mandis. --IANS vg/dan
